chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about Mut'ah (temporary marriage): Is it one of the four (permanent marriages)? He said, 'No, and not even one of the seventy.'

key_terms.السَّبْعِينَ: The seventy (referring to a broader classification of marriage types)

ai.seo_question: Is temporary marriage (Mut'ah) considered one of the four permanent marriages in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the juridical status of Mut'ah by distinguishing it from the four primary permanent marriage types, asserting it is neither one of them nor among the broader seven recognized categories. This distinction underscores the Shia view of Mut'ah as a unique, independent form of marriage with its own specific rulings, rather than a subset of permanent nuptials. The reference to 'seven' likely alludes to the comprehensive classification of marriage types discussed in fiqh literature, emphasizing Mut'ah's distinct legal identity.
